title: Metallic model and materials
summary: Metals are lattices of cations in a sea of delocalized electrons. Explain metal properties, use the bonding triangle to classify materials, and understand alloys and polymers; at HL, transition-metal bonding and condensation polymers.

keyterms.definition: The electrostatic attraction between a lattice of cations and a sea of delocalized electrons.
Valence electrons not attached to any one atom, free to move throughout the metal lattice.
Able to be hammered into shape / drawn into wires; layers of cations slide without breaking the metallic bond.
A diagram plotting electronegativity difference against average electronegativity to locate a binary compound between ionic, covalent and metallic bonding.
A mixture of a metal with other elements; different-sized atoms disrupt the layers, usually making it stronger and harder.
A large molecule made of many repeating units joined covalently.
Joining of unsaturated monomers (alkenes) by opening their C=C bonds, with no other product.
The smallest part of a polymer chain which repeats to make the whole chain.
Joining monomers with two functional groups, eliminating a small molecule (often water) at each link.
A condensation polymer whose monomers are linked by amide groups (–CONH–), e.g. from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid.
A condensation polymer whose monomers are linked by ester groups (–COO–), e.g. from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid.
Both 4s and 3d electrons can be delocalized, giving transition metals high melting points and strong metallic bonding.

options: Delocalized electrons move through the lattice
questions.explanation: Delocalized electrons move when a potential difference is applied.

questions.statement: Metals are malleable because layers of cations can slide over each other while the delocalized electrons keep holding them together.
questions.explanation: Unlike ionic lattices, no repulsion builds up when layers move.

questions.prompt: Why does magnesium have a higher melting point than sodium?
options: Mg²⁺ is smaller and more charged, with more delocalized electrons
questions.explanation: Stronger attraction between smaller, more highly charged cations and more delocalized electrons strengthens metallic bonding.

questions.text: Metallic bonding is the attraction between a lattice of cations and ___ electrons.
questions.explanation: The electrons are not attached to any one atom.

questions.prompt: Order by melting point, lowest first.
questions.explanation: Metallic bond strength rises with smaller cation radius and more delocalized electrons per atom.

questions.statement: Melting points of group 1 metals increase down the group.
questions.explanation: Cations get larger down the group, so attraction to the delocalized electrons weakens and melting points fall.

questions.prompt: Match each property of metals to its explanation.

pairs.right: Strong attraction between cations and electrons

questions.explanation: All metal properties follow from the cation lattice with delocalized electrons.

questions.prompt: Which statement about metals is correct?
options: Metals have shiny surfaces because delocalized electrons interact with light
questions.explanation: Delocalized electrons absorb and re-emit light, giving lustre; metallic bonding is non-directional.

questions.text: Aluminium forms Al³⁺ ions and contributes ___ delocalized electrons per atom.
questions.explanation: Its three valence electrons are delocalized, which strengthens the metallic bond.

questions.prompt: In the bonding triangle, a compound with a large electronegativity difference lies near which vertex?
questions.explanation: Ionic character increases with Δχ, at the top of the triangle.

questions.statement: A binary compound with a low electronegativity difference and a high average electronegativity is mainly covalent.
questions.explanation: For example Cl₂ or CCl₄: both atoms strongly attract electrons, so they share them.

questions.prompt: Why is an alloy usually harder than the pure metal?
options: Different-sized atoms disrupt the layers so they slide less easily
questions.explanation: Atoms of different sizes distort the regular lattice, hindering layer movement.

questions.text: Steel is an alloy of iron and ___.
questions.explanation: Small amounts of carbon greatly increase the hardness and strength of iron.
Addition polymers form from alkenes: the C=C of chloroethene opens to link units.

questions.statement: Addition polymerization produces water as a by-product.
questions.explanation: Addition polymerization forms only the polymer; small molecules are eliminated in condensation polymerization.

questions.text: The repeating unit of poly(propene) is –CH₂–CH(___)–.
questions.explanation: Propene is CH₂=CHCH₃; the methyl group becomes a side group on the chain.

questions.prompt: Match each material to its main bonding type.
questions.explanation: Use bonding type to predict and explain properties of materials.

questions.prompt: Why are many plastics a problem in the environment?
options: Their strong C–C and C–H bonds make them non-biodegradable
questions.explanation: Microorganisms cannot easily break the non-polar backbone, so they persist for a long time.

questions.prompt: Order these binary substances from most ionic to most covalent character.
questions.explanation: Δχ falls: Na–F 3.1, Mg–O 2.1, Al–Cl 1.6, C–Cl 0.6.

questions.prompt: Why do transition metals have high melting points?
options: Both 4s and 3d electrons can be delocalized
questions.explanation: More delocalized electrons and small cations give strong metallic bonding.

questions.prompt: What small molecule is lost when a diol and a dicarboxylic acid form a polyester?
questions.explanation: Each ester link forms from –COOH and –OH, eliminating water.

questions.statement: A polyamide can be made from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid.
questions.explanation: –NH₂ and –COOH react to form amide links, –CONH–, eliminating water.

questions.text: Condensation polymerization requires each monomer to have ___ functional groups.
questions.explanation: Two reactive groups let each monomer link at both ends to form a chain.

questions.prompt: Match each linkage to its polymer type.
questions.explanation: Linkages show how the monomers were joined.

questions.prompt: Proteins are natural examples of which type of polymer?
questions.explanation: Amino acids join by amide (peptide) links in condensation reactions.

questions.statement: Polyesters can be broken down by hydrolysis.
questions.explanation: Water (with acid or base) can split the ester links back to the acid and alcohol; this makes polyesters more degradable than polyalkenes.

questions.text: n monomers of an amino acid joined in a chain release ___ water molecules (for one long chain).
questions.explanation: Each link releases one water; a chain of n units has n − 1 links (≈ n for large n).

questions.prompt: Order the steps in forming one amide link.
items: OH from the acid and H from the amine are removed
questions.explanation: This is a condensation: two molecules join with loss of a small molecule.

questions.prompt: Why is the melting point of iron much higher than that of calcium?
options: Fe has more delocalized electrons from 3d orbitals and a smaller ion
questions.explanation: 3d electrons add to the electron sea, and Fe ions are smaller, strengthening metallic bonding.
